claims.rationale: The cited CISA CPG record (E_23_B21FAA9377991F05) explicitly describes alerting security teams after consecutive unsuccessful login attempts and describes system-enforced policies that prevent future logins for suspicious accounts on IT assets. It also explicitly maps these to the four brute-force subtechniques: T1110.001, T1110.002, T1110.003, and T1110.004.

The cited CISA CPG record (E_23_312B9513BCEE9B9D) recommends MFA for all IT accounts and for accounts and systems in OT environments that can be accessed remotely. It ranks 'Hardware-based, phishing-resistant MFA' first (highest strength) in its sorted list. It further maps the control to 'Brute Force (T1110)', 'Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)', and 'External Remote Services (ICS T0822)'.
